scenes.tts: Stir fresh pineapple into gelatin and chill it, and the gelatin can stay runny. Use canned pineapple, and it sets. Gelatin is a protein. When it cools, its long chains tangle into a net that traps water. What is in fresh pineapple, and what did canning change?
scenes.visual: Two bowls: fresh pineapple stays runny with loose chains, canned sets as the chains tangle into a net; question marks over both.

scenes.tts: Metabolism means all the chemical reactions in a living thing. Many would be far too slow at body temperature without help. The help comes from enzymes, almost all of them proteins, that speed up specific reactions. An enzyme is a catalyst. It speeds up a reaction without being used up.
scenes.visual: A cell outline of reactions, then one reaction with a slow bar that fills fast once an enzyme chip joins it; the enzyme stays.

scenes.tts: Take catalase, an enzyme in potato cells. The substrate is the molecule an enzyme acts on. For catalase, that is hydrogen peroxide. The substrate fits into the active site, a small pocket on the enzyme. The enzyme changes it into products, water and oxygen. The products leave. The enzyme is unchanged and can take in another substrate molecule.
scenes.visual: Enzyme block with a pocket; a substrate piece fits in, becomes two product pieces, they leave, a new substrate arrives.

scenes.tts: Picture a ball that must be pushed over a hill. Activation energy is the energy needed to get a reaction started, like that hill. An enzyme does not add energy. It holds the substrate where bonds break or form more easily. That lowers the hill, so more substrate reacts each second.
scenes.visual: Energy hill sketch with a ball; the hill lowers when the enzyme joins and more balls cross.

scenes.tts: Warmer molecules move faster, so up to a point a warmer reaction runs faster. But too much heat shakes apart the weak attractions that hold the folded chain in shape. To denature is to lose the folded shape a protein needs to work. A denatured enzyme is not dead, but its active site no longer fits. The optimum is the condition where an enzyme works fastest. Most human enzymes have an optimum near thirty-seven degrees Celsius.
scenes.visual: Rate against temperature sketch rises then falls; beside it the enzyme loses its shape and the substrate no longer fits.

scenes.tts: Each enzyme also has a best P H. A change in P H changes electric charges, so substrate and active site may no longer attract. Back to the pineapple. Fresh pineapple contains bromelain, an enzyme that cuts the protein chains in gelatin. Canning heats the fruit enough to denature bromelain. So the canned gelatin sets. The rule: an enzyme works only while its active site keeps its shape.
scenes.visual: A pH strip, then the two bowls again: bromelain cuts chains in fresh; heat denatures bromelain in canned and the net forms.
